title: Rapid point-of-care diagnostics for resistant infections
bottleneck: Clinicians typically wait 24 to 72 hours for culture-based susceptibility results, forcing empiric broad-spectrum antibiotic use that drives resistance. WHO's 2025 diagnostics report identified critical gaps in tests that can rapidly detect priority pathogens and their resistance profiles at the bedside.
why_it_blocks: Without fast diagnostics, stewardship is impossible: doctors cannot prescribe narrowly what they cannot identify quickly.
current_state: Molecular panels and rapid phenotypic tests are improving, but cost, complexity, and limited pathogen coverage keep them out of most clinics worldwide, especially in low-resource settings. The WHO diagnostics report is meant to steer R&D toward the highest-impact tests, but translating guidance into funded products requires market incentives that barely exist for diagnostics. Low-cost, robust tests for low-resource settings are the greatest unmet need.
